data.name: Yagnavalkya
data.gender_notes: Yagnavalkya is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Yagnavalkya is a revered sage in Hindu mythology, known for his profound wisdom and knowledge of Vedic rituals. The name Yagnavalkya carries the meaning “Lord of the Sacrificial Fire” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Yagnavalkya usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the sacrificial fire and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of sacred fire, wisdom, and divine connection.
data.etymology: Yagnavalkya belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the Sacrificial Fire.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Yagnavalkya total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: Yagnavalkya is remembered in Hindu culture as the author of the Yajurveda, one of the four primary Vedas, and the teacher of King Janaka. He conducted a famous 'yajna' or sacrifice, where he taught the 'Upanishads' to his student King Janaka, which transformed Janaka's life, bringing him spiritual enlightenment. Thus, Yagnavalkya is considered a pioneer of Vedic education and a significant figure in Hindu spiritual and cultural history. His influence can still be felt today through the continuing practice of Vedic rituals and teachings.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu spirituality, Yagnavalkya is considered a great sage and a direct link to the divine. He exemplifies knowledge and devotion, and his teachings have inspired countless seekers on their spiritual journey. Yagnavalkya's legacy continues to guide people towards self-realization and the inner connection with the divine. Through the study of his teachings, individuals can deepen their spiritual understanding and tap into the wisdom of thousand-year-old Vedic knowledge.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Yagnavalkya: The name 'Yagnavalkya' symbolizes the deep-rooted knowledge and expertise in the Vedic rituals and sacrifices (Yajnas). He is revered as a sage, a sage of wisdom and a master of rituals. His name signifies one's dedication and devotion towards the Vedic path and its practices.

vedic_reference.note: Mentioned in Brihadaranyaka Upanishad as a great sage

historical_references.reference: Yagnavalkya was a renowned sage and philosopher, known for his extensive knowledge of the Vedas and the performance of the Vedic rituals. He is believed to have lived around 1200 BCE during the later Vedic period.
historical_references.context: Philosopher and sage, extensive knowledge of the Vedas, performance of Vedic rituals

historical_references.reference: Yagnavalkya is also remembered for his dialogue with King Janaka, during which he expounded upon the concept of the self (Atman) and the nature of reality. This dialogue is recorded in the Upanishads, specifically the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad.
historical_references.context: Philosopher, dialogue with King Janaka, expounded upon the concept of the self (Atman) and the nature of reality
